property_summary: The Collect function always succeeds when it reduces the sender's balance, regardless of gas provided to the recipient.
The user's balance never increases after a successful Collect call, regardless of gas provided to the recipient.
After Collect, the caller's balance in Acc is never greater than before the call, regardless of gas provided to the recipient.
After a successful Collect call, the sender's balance in Acc is reduced by exactly the withdrawn amount, regardless of gas provided to the recipient.
The caller's balance in Acc after a Collect call is always equal to their balance before the call minus the amount requested, regardless of whether the recipient reverts or runs out of gas.
The Collect function should only allow withdrawal when the sender's balance is at least MinSum.
After Collect reverts or succeeds, the sender's balance in Acc cannot go below MinSum unless the transaction reverts.
After a successful Collect, the final balance of the sender is not negative and any decrease is exactly the amount withdrawn.
After Collect reverts or succeeds, the sender's balance in Acc is always at least MinSum.
Collect should only succeed when sender's balance is at least MinSum.
It is always possible to withdraw the entire balance when the balance is exactly equal to MinSum after the unlock time.
After any sequence of Put and Collect calls, the balance of a user is always greater than or equal to MinSum if the unlock time has passed and the balance before the Collect was at least MinSum.
When the balance is exactly equal to MinSum, the Collect function should still succeed in transferring the amount if the other conditions are met.
When balance equals MinSum and other conditions hold, Collect always successfully transfers the requested amount.
If the user's balance is exactly MinSum and the collect amount is equal to MinSum, the call to Collect should not revert.
After Collect, the reentrancy lock ensures that locked_ becomes false, which means a subsequent Collect call can succeed.
After a successful Collect call that decreases the sender's balance, the recorded unlockTime for that sender remains unchanged.
After a Collect call that succeeds, the first argument to the next Collect call can be the same as before and succeed.
Successive Collect calls with the same parameters will succeed if the first one succeeds.
The sum of all balances across all accounts equals the contract's balance after any sequence of operations.
The Collect function should revert when called by an address with insufficient balance.
The Collect function should revert when called with a non-zero amount by an address that never made a Put deposit.
Collect should revert when the caller has no balance, regardless of the amount.
Collect should revert when called by an address that has no pending deposit (Acc[caller].balance == 0).
After any sequence of public interactions, a call to Collect should revert if the caller's balance is zero.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, the balance of the caller is non-negative.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the balance of the caller is either reduced by the collected amount or unchanged, depending on whether the condition (balance >= MinSum) holds.

After a call to Collect(uint256) that succeeds, the returned value (boolean) is always true if the caller's balance is at least MinSum and the caller's balance is at least the requested amount and block.timestamp > unlockTime, otherwise it is false.

After a call to Collect(uint256), MinSum remains unchanged (P.MinSum() == M.MinSum() fails because P.MinSum() == 1 ether and M.MinSum() == 2 ether, but the rule is that MinSum is always equal to the current value set at deployment). The invariant is that collectability threshold MinSum stays constant.
After any call to Collect(uint _am), if the collected amount is less than MinSum, the caller's balance remains unchanged.
